notes: The session's web search allowance ran out after twelve searches (the five legislative candidates, the two county attorneys, the sheriff and the Minneapolis school board race). Everything else was found by reading known addresses directly: the campaign websites filed with the Secretary of State (already in sl_websites), each government's own site, and the state DFL's list. No search engine was read in place of the search tool. This machine's address lookups failed often, so several sites were out of reach.

No findings (left blank rather than guessed): Daniel Bergstrom (Becker County's site leaves a certificate out and was not read with checking off), Dawn L. Johansen (not on Grant County's commissioners page), David Mills (Cook County's robots.txt asks scripts to stay out; not requested), Bob Schuldt (Houston County's site refused the secure handshake), Tanya Huffman (not on Farmington's council page), Patrick Cusack (not on North Mankato's council page), Emmeline Bartnes (not on the Detroit Lakes board page), John Magnuson (the Fergus Falls district site showed no board page to a script), Stephanie Johnson (not on the Minneapolis DFL's list of endorsed school board candidates; no campaign site found), and the two judges, Jeffrey M Johnson and Laura A. Pietan (the Judicial Branch site refuses scripts and was not requested).

Dawn Loberg: KNSI Radio and St. Cloud Live report that Republican delegates endorsed her for House District 13B, but no party page of its own stating that was found, so no endorsement is recorded. John R. Jasinski: no party page stating a 2026 endorsement was found.
Allen Andersen's birth year is worked out from a newspaper's line of October 20, 2022 ("32. (Turns 33 on 10/31)"), which gives 1989; only the year is kept.

Two filed campaign sites still show an earlier campaign (John R. Jasinski's title says District 24; Brad Johnson's says "VOTE NOV 8th" and 2022). Each names the candidate and the office; the 'how' says so, and whether to show them is for the verifier and John.
Brad Johnson's county page was read as far as "served as manager on the Coon Creek Watershed District Boa..." (the line was cut by the reader); the verifier should confirm the body's full name.

Verifier, 2026-10-02: every address was re-opened. Corrected wording: Lindsey Port's site description (title as the page gives it; no mention of where the committee is), Amanda Matchett's site description and quote (the page's words are "DFL-Endorsed Candidate for House District 32A", in the home page's title), and Jessica Olstad's site description (the site never gives her surname). John R. Jasinski's site still carries District 24 in its title, as the researcher said. Brad Johnson's county page gives the body's full name as "Coon Creek Watershed District Board of Managers".

website.how: The site's title is "Re-elect John Jasinski for Minnesota State Senate District 24" and it calls itself his "Official campaign website"; its text speaks of representing "the people of District 19". The title still carries the number his district had before 2023 (the Legislative Reference Library lists him in District 24 for 2017-2022 and District 19 since 2023), so the site has not been rewritten for 2026. It is the address filed with the Secretary of State.

The site's title is "Re-elect Senate Lindsey Port"; it reads "Senator Lindsey Port fights for what's right" and "Join our campaign to re-elect Lindsey", names Senate District 55, and its footer reads "Paid for by Lindsey Port for MN". It is the address filed with the Secretary of State.
